level_rationale: Eight months of thick yellow toenails on both big toes with crumbly distal tips today in a 68-year-old adult describes chronic bilateral hallux nail dystrophy warranting a non-urgent outpatient general-physician visit for diagnostic nail testing and targeted therapy rather than emergency care, whereas developing red streaks spreading up from those dystrophic big toes today signals acute ascending bacterial lymphangitis requiring immediate ER evaluation and systemic antibiotic therapy.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 68, 8 months of thick yellow toenails on both big toes, and crumbly nail tips today without naming onychomycosis or fungal infection, with a 1-word span difference (19 vs 18 words) and identical digit multisets across all 5 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, replacing f3 ('and their tips are crumbly') with 'and red streaks started spreading up from those big toes' stays within the same dystrophic big-toe skin-barrier case without adding laterality or new body-part nouns, escalating care from outpatient doctor evaluation (level 2) to ER treatment for ascending bacterial lymphangitis (level 4).
